channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Involuntary manslaughter investigation opened following deadly fire in Schaerbeek
item.description: A Ugandan woman in her forties died in the blaze alongside her 18-year-old daughter, according to unconfirmed reports in Belgian media.

item.title: Brussels firefighters call off strike but warn they will resume if demands aren't met
item.description: The strike, which began on 21 July, was launched over what unions described as structural staff shortages and chronic underfunding at the Fire and Emergency Medical Aid Service (SAIMU).

item.title: Why do we have such a visceral response to the ugliness of Schuman Square?
item.description: The Schuman roundabout was expected to be bold and distinctive, but at some point along the line, someone said, "scratch that".

item.title: Everything you need to know about public transport disruptions in north Brussels this summer ​
item.description: As many people swap Brussels for sunnier climes over the summer, public transport operator STIB-MIVB is carrying out maintenance works.

item.title: Couleur Café faces 'major financial blow' after storm cancellation
item.description: "Our priority is to find a fair solution without jeopardising the festival’s survival," the festival organisers said on Friday.

item.title: West Nile virus cases increase across Europe, WHO warns
item.description: In severe cases, patients can develop a high fever, neck stiffness, confusion or paralysis.

item.title: What to do in Brussels this weekend: 24 - 26 July
item.description: While Belgian National Day festivities may be over, Brussels isn't slowing down. Here are some of our top picks for enjoying what the capital has to offer!

item.title: Property tax rise to be sharpest in eight Brussels municipalities
item.description: The Brussels-Capital Region has begun sending out property tax notices for 2026, with bills set to rise the highest in eight municipalities.

item.title: Brussels residents urged to moderate tap water use after drought alert
item.description: The Brussels Region’s regional ‘drought’ task force activated the yellow alert – the drought vigilance phase – on Thursday.

item.title: Brussels for kids: What to do with your family this weekend – 25 to 26 July
item.description: In Brussels, summer is never quiet, even in the three weeks between Belgian National Day and the 15 August holiday. Here are our favourite picks for family-centred fun!

item.title: One person stabbed near Brussels-Midi station
item.description: The investigation is continuing to identify the attacker in the incident on Boulevard du Midi.

item.title: Brussels cultural centre forced to close after car crashes into façade
item.description: The Jules Verne Centre in Forest said on Thursday that the damage was so severe that it had to cancel all scheduled events.

item.title: Bad Bunny treats Brussels to Stromae classic on last show of world tour
item.description: For 2,5 hours, the Puerto Rican artist did not speak a word of English, but he did treat the fans to a little bit of Belgian culture.

item.title: These are Belgium's most popular names – how common is yours?
item.description: Belgium's most common first names are declining, but you can now look up how popular your name.

item.title: 'I refuse to give up': Woman left heartbroken after cat disappears at Brussels Airport
item.description: “Mishu is not just a pet, he is a member of our family. We are devastated and desperately want to bring him home."

item.title: Brussels Airport invest nearly €6 million in specialised fire engines
item.description: In the event of an incident on the tarmac, firefighters must reach the scene within three minutes, with at least three crash tenders deployed.

item.title: Brussels emergency services remain disrupted as firefighters' strike continues
item.description: Firefighters have urged the public to be extra cautious and, where possible, avoid activities that carry a high risk of fire, accident or injury.

item.title: How Brussels became a French-speaking city

item.title: From Schuman to Midi: How the Brussels 'master architect' wants a quality city
item.description: "Ugliness is not an argument. What do we need? How do we use the resources that are there?"
